command: SCORED_FROM=records/scored/authoring-expert-run-1.json SCORED_KEPT=<kept folders> SCORED_JUDGE_MODEL=claude-fable-5-2 SCORED_SESSION_LIMIT=3 SCORED_CLAUDE=<another Claude Code> CK3_GAME_PATH=<game dir> task scored:rejudge
notes: Every authoring session, the agent server, the checker and the expectations read the base game at <game dir>, build 1.21.0.3.

Each trial is one authoring test session of the Claude Code installed on the machine the run was made on, given the request in a fresh copy of its base mod with the agent server and the skills, then one judge test session given the request and what the first left; the script gave neither session credentials, and pychivalry itself makes no model call.

Grade one is pychivalry's checker on the result: errors, warnings and whether it is in pychivalry's format, each a measure of its own. Grade two is the request's expectations, checked in code, and the judge's answer on each judged dimension. A trial whose harness did not hold is listed and not counted. The record states measures only: the owner's targets (docs/decisions.md, decision 127) are read from them, by the run when it ends and by task scored:targets.

Trials were added on 2026-11-25 by a run continuing the record (SCORED_CONTINUE=true) at commit 3c2c615808eb290b2191cf1be36dbda2d1d1a06c, made the same way as the record's first (made 2026-11-25 at commit 4860cf0c290ac17bbb0c995ca57730c26b6aa183): the same request list, prompts, judge, base mods, skills, Claude Code version, models, limits, arguments and agent server; between the two commits only documents, records, tests and the run's own files changed (Taskfile.yml, tools/src/cli.ts, tools/src/scored-run/authoring-targets.ts, tools/src/scored-run/authoring-testing.ts, tools/src/scored-run/authoring.ts, tools/src/scored-run/continuation.ts, tools/src/scored-run/fake-claude.ts, tools/src/scored-run/stop-rule.ts).

A trial whose harness did not hold is listed with its reasons, graded, and judged when its authoring session ended by itself; it is left out of every measure and never counted as a success. When the targets are read, such a trial whose session ended by itself counts against each target its own result fails, and one whose session broke counts for nothing. The run carries on after it unless a session was not set up as the run asks, the run's first trial broke, or three trials in a row did not hold; a run continuing the record tries its request again.

Re-judged on 2026-11-25 by task scored:rejudge at commit d855cb1269e79a53d62b3866a1fdab93f674fb97, starting no authoring session: the trials' sessions, results and grades are those of records/scored/authoring-expert-run-1.json (its tool, time and notes above), each result read from its run's kept trial folder and graded again over the same game and spec package with the record's validity and expectations to the letter; only the judge was run again (61 judge test sessions of Claude Code 2.1.330), with version 2 of the judge's prompt (tools/scored-run/judge.prompt.md, sha256 766c318c92d3f1ec8b75e7b64200ad815ed65fa8cb396049d29975d4117fbdaa): the request, its questions and the result, with what pychivalry's checker reports in the result over the installed game and the game's own description of every trigger, effect, iterator and link the result writes, from which it takes whether a name exists and what it means, never from memory. Judged now and not by its run, by the run's rule of today (a trial whose authoring session was set up as asked and ended by itself is judged, also when it did not hold for what it did): event-county-unrest trial 4.
